 AWAR D Preface 1.

Detailed Accident Report (DAR) seeking compensation for bodily injury sustained in road accident has been filed along with copy of Final Report under section 279/337 IPC & 146/196 M.V.
Act in FIR No.119/2017 PS Kapashera, Delhi.
Background 2.

Brief facts culled from Final Report filed along with DAR would reveal that Prahlad selling Watermelons near Farm No. 69, Pushpanjali Gate, Bijwasan-Najafgarh Road sustained bodily injury in motor vehicle accident on 03.04.2017 at around 1:00 pm after one Silver colour Hyundai Accent Car No. DL-4SCS- 0462 driven at high speed in rash and negligent manner hit against his Cart.
Respondent Sonu Kumar apprehended at the spot called PCR on 100 number and took injured to AIIMs Trauma Centre where nature of injury upon MLC No.500015355 was opined simple.
3. FIR No.119/2017 under section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Kapashera on 03.04.2017 and Sonu Kumar (driver-cum-owner) formally arrested on 05.05.2017 was released on police bail.

Hyundai Accent Car No. DL-4CS-0462 seized by the IO was released to respondent Sonu Kumar on superdari after mechanical inspection and IO thereafter concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/337 IPC & 146/196 of Prahlad vs Sonu Kumar on 6 February, 2025

3 M.V. Act.
Defence 4.

Respondent Sonu Kumar (driver-cum-owner) has disputed liability to pay compensation by contending that injured Prahlad selling watermelons on the road suddenly came in front of the Car and respondent driving the vehicle at very normal speed could not avoid the accident despite his best efforts.

Inquiry 5. Following issues were settled on on 05.01.2018 and matter was posted for petitioner's evidence.
i.
Whether Prahlad sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 03.4.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL4CS-0462 being driven and owned by respondent no.1 Sonu Kumar?
.... OPP ii.
Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
... OPP iii.
Relief.

6. PW-1 Prahlad in paras 1 to 5 of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A has inter alia deposed about - (i) multiple injury sustained in road accident near Farm No. 69, Pushpanjali Gate, Bijwasan- Najafgarh Road on 03.04.2017 at around 1:00 pm after his vegetable trolley was hit by offending vehicle driven in rash and negligent manner; (ii) treatment at local hospital & JPN, Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, Delhi from 04.04.2017 till 12.04.2017;
(iii) expenses incurred on treatment; (iv) monthly income Rs.20,000/- by selling vegetables AND (v) general and special damages on account of bodily injury sustained in road accident.

7. His cross-examination by Ld. counsel for respondent has been recorded on 08.10.2018 and petitioners' evidence was closed on 02.04.2019.
8.

Sh. Sonu Kumar (driver-cum-owner) has tendered affidavit Ex.R1W1/A in evidence by contending that injured Prahlad selling watermelons on the busy road suddenly came in front of the Car and accident could not be avoided despite his best efforts.

He has adverted to copy of driving licence Ex.R1W1/1.
9.

Cross-examination of respondent by Ld. counsel for injured has been recorded and respondents'
evidence was closed on 17.12.2019.
Discussion and Conclusion
10. Advocate Sh. B.K. Pandey for injured has addressed submissions.
11. I have carefully perused pleadings and evidence adduced on judicial file.

My issue wise finding is recorded below:
12.

...OPP 13. PW-1 Prahlad in para 2 of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A has deposed about bodily injury sustained in road accident on 03.04.2017 at around 1:00 pm as a result of rash and negligent driving of respondent Sonu Kumar.
14. His testimony has remained consistent and suggestion disputing negligence of the driver has been denied by insisting that offending vehicle had hit injured from behind.

15. Involvement of Hyundai Accent Car No. DL-4SCS-0462 in motor vehicle accident has not been disputed by respondent Sonu Kumar who nonetheless has contended that injured Prahlad selling Watermelons on the busy road suddenly came in front of the Car and he could not avoid the accident despite best efforts.

16. It is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
17.

entities.text:
Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below :
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a praticular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimaints were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."

18. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.

22. No other document has been filed on record or relied in evidence to show any other injury.
MEDICINES AND TREATMENT 23.
PW-1 Prahlad in para 4 of affidavit has deposed about regular treatment after being discharged from hospital.

However, neither any Discharge Summary verifying treatment at JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMs, Delhi from 04.04.2017 to 12.04.2017 nor any Bill/Cash Memo verifying expenses incurred on treatment has been adduced in evidence.
He is, therefore, not entitled to any amount under the head - Medicines & Treatment.
CONVEYANCE AND SPECIAL DIET 24.
Injured Prahlad having suffered bodily injury in motor vehicle accident was taken to Deepan Hospital from where he was referred to JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMs, Delhi.
It is assumed that he might have used private vehicle/hired taxi for medical examination/treatment at JPN Apex Traum Centre, AIIMs, Delhi.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.2,000/- (Rupees Two Thousand only) is awarded towards conveyance, in addition, to Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) towards special diet for recovery from simple injury.
ATTENDANT CHARGES 25.

It is assumed that Prahlad having suffered laceration over right leg and scrotum might have needed an attendant for a month even if such gratuitous service was rendered by some or the other of his family/relatives.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs.
Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some of his family member.

LOSS OF INCOME 26.
PW-1 Prahlad in para 5 of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A has deposed to be earning Rs.20,000/- per month by selling vegetables.
A nominal sum of Rs.5000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) is awarded under the head Loss of Income in the absence of treatment record.
PAIN AND SUFFERING 27.

Following factors are to be taken into account for assessing compensation under the head - Pain and Suffering:

New India
Assurance Co.
Ltd. & Anr. (2010)
10 SCC 254 has observed that whole idea in case of assessment of all damages for personal injury is to put the claimant in the same position as he was insofar as money can.

Perfect compensation is hardly possible but one has to keep in mind that the victim has done no wrong; he has suffered at the hands of wrongdoer and Court must take care to give him full and fair compensation for that he had suffered.
29. Sh. Prahlad having suffered laceration over right leg and scrotum was examined at JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, Delhi on 03.04.2017 and nature of injury was opined simple.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Respondent Sonu Kumar apprehended at the spot called PCR on 100 number and took injured to AIIMs Trauma Centre where nature of injury upon MLC No.500015355 was opined simple.
3. FIR No.119/2017 under section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Kapashera on 03.04.2017 and Sonu Kumar (driver-cum-owner) formally arrested on 05.05.2017 was released on police bail.
Hyundai Accent Car No. DL-4CS-0462 seized by the IO was released to respondent Sonu Kumar on superdari after mechanical inspection and IO thereafter concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/337 IPC & 146/196 of Prahlad vs Sonu Kumar on 6 February, 2025
Respondent Sonu Kumar (driver-cum-owner) has disputed liability to pay compensation by contending that injured Prahlad selling watermelons on the road suddenly came in front of the Car and respondent driving the vehicle at very normal speed could not avoid the accident despite his best efforts.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
16. It is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
17.
18. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
He is, therefore, not entitled to any amount under the head - Medicines & Treatment.
Injured Prahlad having suffered bodily injury in motor vehicle accident was taken to Deepan Hospital from where he was referred to JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMs, Delhi.
It is assumed that he might have used private vehicle/hired taxi for medical examination/treatment at JPN Apex Traum Centre, AIIMs, Delhi.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.2,000/- (Rupees Two Thousand only) is awarded towards conveyance, in addition, to Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) towards special diet for recovery from simple injury.
It is assumed that Prahlad having suffered laceration over right leg and scrotum might have needed an attendant for a month even if such gratuitous service was rendered by some or the other of his family/relatives.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs.
Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some of his family member.
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 9 of Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible but one has to keep in mind that the victim has done no wrong; he has suffered at the hands of wrongdoer and Court must take care to give him full and fair compensation for that he had suffered.
30. Compensation for (i) loss of future earning/prospects AND (ii) non pecuniary damages including loss of amenities and loss of expectation of life is not required to be assessed in the absence of serious injury resulting in permanent physical disability.
There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest on the award amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
It would be apposite to award him a sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) towards Pain & Suffering.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the present case, it will be just and proper to grant interest @ 7.5%
per annum on the award amount in terms of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mannat Johar & Anr. (2019) 15 SCC 260.
Injured Prahlad is therefore awarded interest @ 7.5% per annum upon award amount Rs.22,000/- from the date of filing of DAR on 18.05.2017 till notice of deposit under Order XXI Rule 1 CPC.
Respondent Sonu Kumar driving Hyundai Accent Car No. DL-4SCS-0462 in rash and negligent manner resulting in bodily injury sustained in road accident shall pay compensation amount with interest to injured Prahlad.
34. FINDING : Issue No.2 is decided accordingly by holding that Sonu Kumar shall pay compensation amount with interest to injured Prahlad.
RELIEF 35.
In view of foregoing discussion and observations and having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, award for a sum of Rs.22,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR on 18.05.2017 till notice of deposit under Order XXI Rule 1 CPC is passed in favour of injured Prahald.
